title: How Liminalism Became the Defining Aesthetic of Our Time
summary: An exploration of how liminalism—the aesthetic of in-between spaces like empty airports, motel corridors, and abandoned malls—has emerged as the defining visual language of contemporary culture, reflecting collective anxiety about transition, uncertainty, and the dissolution of clear social boundaries in modern life.
problem_solved: Explains why transitional and ambiguous spaces resonate so deeply with contemporary audiences experiencing constant uncertainty
why_valuable: Provides insight into how art and design aesthetics mirror and shape collective cultural psychology in times of social transition
